perf.summary: Cache ptr[i] in the descending j-scan instead of re-loading and re-comparing through CompareTo each iteration.
perf.currentCost: The j-loop calls ptr[j].CompareTo(ptr[i]) each step, reloading ptr[i] (the pivot) every iteration and going through the IComparable<T> interface comparison.
perf.proposedChange: T pivot = ptr[i]; while (ptr[j].CompareTo(pivot) <= 0) j--; - hoist the invariant pivot load out of the loop. Same pattern applies to the i-scan where ptr[i+1] vs ptr[i] could reuse one loaded value across steps.
perf.rationale: Removes a redundant load per iteration and shortens the dependency chain on the pivot; the value of ptr[i] is loop-invariant in the j-scan.
perf.risk: None for the j-scan (ptr[i] is not modified there). For T being a generic unmanaged struct, CompareTo on IComparable<T> may still not inline under Burst; consider an il2cpp/Burst-friendly constrained call, but that is orthogonal. Identical results.
